subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: Match future forms with offers, predictions and arrangements.
Use home technology words, phrasal verbs and advice phrases.
Review personality adjectives and present tenses from earlier units.

tf.s: 'I'll carry those books for you' is an offer.
tf.why: Yes! We often use will for offers.

tf.s: 'I'm seeing the doctor at four this afternoon' is a prediction.
tf.why: It is an arrangement: a fixed plan with a time.

tf.s: We can use the present continuous for future arrangements.
tf.why: Right, like 'I'm meeting Ali on Friday'.

tf.s: We say 'Our electricity often goes off during a storm.'
tf.why: Yes, 'go off' means stop working here.

tf.s: We use a kettle to wash clothes.
tf.why: A kettle boils water; a washing machine washes clothes.

tf.s: Stative verbs like 'understand' are usually used in the continuous form.
tf.why: Stative verbs usually take the present simple: 'Do you understand?'

tf.s: Adverbs of frequency go after the verb be.
tf.why: Good: 'Osama is never late for school.'

tf.s: A sociable person enjoys being with other people.
tf.why: Yes, a sociable person loves company.

tf.s: The correct phrase is 'keen at football'.
'Brilliant at' is a correct adjective + preposition pair.

o: I'll help you with your bag.
boxes.why: An offer is when you say you will do something for someone.
A fridge-freezer keeps food cold or frozen.

boxes.q: Complete: Please switch ___ the TV. I'm going to bed.
boxes.why: We switch off a machine to stop it.

boxes.q: Complete: How ___ watching a film tonight?
Which word means 'looking very real, like life'?

boxes.why: The action is happening now, so we use the present continuous.

o: Osama is never late for school.
Osama never is late for school.
Osama is late never for school.

boxes.q: Complete the advice: You ___ ask your teacher for help.
Which word means 'what you like more'?
boxes.why: Your preference is the thing you like better.

hunt.q: 'I'll carry those books for you' is…
She loves being with friends. She's…

mcq.q: What is the function of 'I'm meeting my friends at the mall at five'?
mcq.why: It is a fixed plan with a time, so it is an arrangement.

mcq.q: Which word means 'something difficult that tests your skill'?
mcq.why: A challenge is a hard task that tests you.

mcq.q: Which phrasal verb means 'start a machine'?
mcq.why: We switch on a machine to start it.

mcq.q: Which of these is a stative verb?
mcq.why: 'Understand' describes a state, not an action.

mcq.q: Your friend is carrying a heavy box. What do you say?
mcq.why: We use will for an offer made at the moment of speaking.

o: Fatima and Raya play volleyball now and then.
Fatima and Raya play now and then volleyball.
Fatima and Raya now and then volleyball play.
Now and then volleyball Fatima and Raya play.
mcq.why: Time phrases like 'now and then' usually go at the end.

mcq.q: Complete: I'm not keen ___ cooking, but I'm brilliant ___ drawing.
Why is 'I'm not thinking that's a good idea' wrong?
o: 'Think' is an opinion here, so we use the present simple.
We must use the past simple.
mcq.why: For opinions we say 'I don't think…'.

mcq.q: Look at those dark clouds! Which sentence fits best?
mcq.why: We use 'going to' when we can see what will happen.

mcq.q: A student writes: 'I learnt phrasal verbs well. I need to revise will and be going to.' What is the student doing?
mcq.why: Great! Thinking about what you know helps you plan your revision.
